title: Numbers with from_chars
description:
Parse numbers using `std::from_chars` exactly as its page describes.

```
"42"     -> 42 (all characters used)
"42abc"  -> 42 (stopped at 'a')
"abc"    -> invalid_argument
"99999999999" -> result_out_of_range
```
hints: `ec == std::errc{}` means success; `ec == std::errc::invalid_argument` and `std::errc::result_out_of_range` are the two failures (lesson 2.02).
`ptr == text.data() + text.size()` tells whether everything was read.
requirements: Check `ec` and `ptr` from the result, as the "Return value" section explains.
Report whether all the input was used.
Note in a comment two ways `from_chars` differs from `std::stoi` (it does not skip spaces and does not throw).
stretch: Parse hexadecimal with the `base` argument and floating point with the `double` overload.
